# OpenAdapt

> A person, or a computer-use agent once, shows a task in an application with no usable API. OpenAdapt compiles it into a program that makes the same entry every time with no model calls, confirms the right record before acting, reads the saved record back from the system of record, and stops instead of improvising or retrying.

This is the llms.txt for the OpenAdapt monorepo (github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt). Start with the capability map: https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/CAPABILITIES.md. It lists every capability with its status (released, in review, planned), its evidence (real app, synthetic, untested) and where it lives. Check it before concluding that OpenAdapt lacks something.

## Capabilities in brief (openadapt-flow 2.2.0)

- Compile one or more demonstrations into a program: `record`, `compile`, `induce` (one branching program from several recordings), `disambiguate`, `teach-branch` (a branch learned from several halts), `for-each` (a worklist).
- Before acting, confirm the right record: page structure first, then template, OCR and geometry; a complete known-ID list lifts look-alike stops (`known-ids`).
- After saving, read the record back independently: API, database, FHIR (including SMART Backend Services), or a separate session. `verify-run` judges any executor's write the same way. Uncertain saves end in RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED and are never retried.
- Each save waits for a person by default; answer on a paired phone (OpenAdapt Desktop). Person-signed grants can let named agents answer.
- Surfaces: web (released), native Windows and macOS (early), RDP (early; Aardwolf or headless FreeRDP), Citrix (exploratory). `compose` and `process` chain programs across surfaces; one program that switches surfaces mid-run is in review.
- Fastest layer: page structure first; steps can run as direct API calls (`ApiActuator`); compiling captured network traffic into API calls automatically is planned.
- When the app changes: governed `repair`, agent-demonstrated fixes for a halted run, layout-drift halts, fleet drift patches with no patient data; self-repair (an agent proposes, Flow probes up to the save, a person approves) is in progress.
- Computer-use agents: `openadapt_flow.jit` compiles an agent's successful run into a program; admission by a person, an admitter key, or an agent under a person-signed policy.
- Inputs from documents: `intake` fills a workflow's inputs from a referral PDF, fax image or email.
- Proof and privacy: Seals (signed, countersigned, timestamped, offline by default), strict no-outbound mode, an unattended on-prem service, PHI redaction (openadapt-privacy; opt-in today).
- Recording: openadapt-capture records input, video and accessibility trees on one clock (Windows, macOS, Linux X11), including a background shadow mode.

The MCP server section follows; the other packages are listed at the end.

## MCP server: openadapt-agent (`uvx openadapt-agent serve --bundles <dir>`, MCP Registry `io.github.OpenAdaptAI/openadapt-agent`)

> Your AI agent decides what to enter. OpenAdapt enters it in the app and checks that it saved.

Use this when an AI agent has decided what to enter in an app with no usable API, such as an EMR, a payer portal, or a desktop or Citrix app. OpenAdapt enters the values in the same screens staff use, on a computer the customer controls, then reads the saved record back. When something doesn't match, it stops and a person decides. A normal run makes no AI model calls.

## The contract: three tools

- `list_workflows`: each workflow's `name`, `purpose`, `done_means`, and typed `inputs` (types, enums, formats).
- `run_workflow(workflow, inputs, request_id, wait_seconds?)`: one piece of work. `request_id` is the caller's own id and is required. The same `request_id` returns the latest result and never writes twice.
- `get_run(run_id, wait_seconds?)`: the result of a run that returned `outcome: running`.

Every result has `outcome`, `safe_to_retry`, `what_happened` (one plain sentence), `next_action`, `proof`, `run_id`, and `request_id`. Tools publish an MCP `outputSchema` and return `structuredContent`.

## Outcomes (the honesty rules)

- `done`: saved and checked by reading the record back. `proof` is `local` (checked on the customer's computer), `sealed` (signed receipt), or `simulated` (sandbox, no app opened). A verified local run is done; it is never reported as an error.
- `needs_review`: stopped before a save; a person decides. Nothing was written, unless `record_changed` is `unknown` (a run waiting for a person to approve a save may have made an earlier one). Don't start the same work again.
- `not_sure_if_saved`: a save may have gone through. Never retry. A person checks the record. Never tell the user nothing changed.
- `did_not_run`: this call wrote nothing. Fix the cause and retry with the same `request_id` when `safe_to_retry` is true. After `request_id_conflict`, an earlier request with the same `request_id` may have saved; call `get_run` with `first_run_id` to see it.

Only `done` is a success. Results come from openadapt-flow's `transaction_outcome`, never from the coarse halt label alone.

## Try it

`openadapt-agent serve` with no flags is a sandbox: one workflow, `add_triage_note`, on MockMed, a synthetic clinic app. The `sandbox_case` input picks the outcome: `normal` (done), `duplicate_record` (needs_review), `false_saved_banner` and `timeout_after_save` (not_sure_if_saved), `app_offline` (did_not_run). Install the `tutorial` extra to drive the synthetic app with the real engine; otherwise results are simulated and say so.

- From PyPI: `claude mcp add --scope user openadapt -- uvx --python 3.12 openadapt-agent serve`. This only registers the server; Claude Code starts it at the next `claude` session. Then ask it to run `add_triage_note` with a made-up note and a request id.
- Requires openadapt-flow 2.2.0 or later, which is on PyPI and installs with openadapt-agent.

## Modes and older surfaces

- `openadapt-agent serve --mode production --bundles <dir>`: run an operator's compiled workflows through the governed `openadapt-flow run` CLI. `--bundles <dir>` alone stays read-only. `--mode attended` adds decisions on paused runs by a person at that computer. `--mode sandbox` is the default without `--bundles`.
- Older flags still work: `--allow-run` (same as `--mode production` with `--bundles`, or the sandbox without), `--tutorial` (the sandbox), `--allow-attended-actions` (part of `--mode attended`).
- Older tools stay registered with `--bundles`: `get_workflow`, `get_run_report`, `list_needs_attention`, `get_attention_item`, and deprecated per-workflow `run_workflow_<opaque-id>` tools (no request id; they now also return `outcome` and `safe_to_retry`).
- Attended actions: `continue_attention` (after a person completes the paused task; Flow rechecks and resumes without repeating it), `skip_attention` (declared skip only), `reject_attention` (ends the run; earlier steps may still have effects), `teach_attention`, `escalate_attention`. Each needs an exact capability digest, a stable idempotency key, a confirmation, and MCP form elicitation; otherwise use Flow's attended console.
- `openadapt-agent serve --authoring`: local first-demo tools `observe`, `start_record`, `click`, `halt`, and more over stdio. It doesn't enable runs and opens no HTTP listener. `openadapt-agent authoring connect <openadapt://runner or pack URL>`: outbound mailbox client for hosted ChatGPT.com and Claude.ai. Local stdio recording also drives native Windows apps through Flow's Windows agent server (`--windows-agent-url`; the agent may run on another computer, such as a Mac) and RDP or Citrix client windows from pixels (`--remote-window`, `--remote-window-title`, `--citrix`). Screens are off unless the operator passes `--authoring-screens scrubbed` or `unscrubbed`. Each step is marked `actor` agent or person, and a person accepts the recording. Guide: https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/blob/main/packages/flow/docs/RECORDING_ON_WINDOWS_RDP_CITRIX.md. Hosted chats can't click the user's GUI; send them to the job box at https://openadapt.ai/#job-box. The job page it makes has **Connect this computer**, which gives the runner link. Through Desktop they guide a person on native Windows, RDP, and Citrix. Hosted MCP is `https://openadapt.ai/mcp`.
- `openadapt-agent emit-skill <bundle> --out <dir>`: a PHI-safe Agent Skill per workflow (no recorded values, step text, or secrets; one description per workflow).

## Workflow cards

An operator can add `openadapt-card.json` next to a bundle's `workflow.json` with `name`, `purpose`, `done_means`, and input descriptions. Card text reaches the calling agent; it must not contain patient details.

## Product state

Standard and Regulated runs need a workflow admission; Demo and the synthetic sandbox may run without one. Target admissions: https://openadapt.ai/production-lifecycle.json (seven, remote-safe-synthetic). Workflow admissions: https://openadapt.ai/production-workflow-admissions.json (seven, 0.0.0-synthetic, not a customer job). A missing or expired admission means not actively admitted.

## Public capability vs private artifact

- The package and MCP server are the public OpenAdapt capability. Install from PyPI as `openadapt-agent`.
- A customer's compiled workflow bundle is their private artifact, supplied at server start with `--bundles`. It is never embedded in the package, `server.json`, or any registry listing. The sandbox generates its synthetic workflow on the fly.

## Other OpenAdapt packages

- [openadapt-flow](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/flow) (`pip install openadapt-flow`): records a task, compiles it into a deterministic workflow, replays it and checks the result. The core package; `openadapt-flow[agent]` adds the MCP server code.
- [openadapt-types](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt/tree/main/packages/types) (`pip install openadapt-types`): the portable contracts, now `openadapt_flow.contracts`; this name is kept as a compatibility shim.
- [openadapt](https://github.com/OpenAdaptAI/OpenAdapt) (`pip install openadapt`): the launcher CLI.
